sources.title: Leftovers: cool and cover leftovers and put them in a fridge or freezer within 2 hours; store below 5 C; eat within 3 days; cooked rice and pasta within 2 days; freeze up to 3 months; throw away leftovers out of the fridge more than 4 hours; reheat to steaming hot (at least 60 C); never reheat rice and pasta more than once; the 2-hour/4-hour time is cumulative. Re-read 2026-10-29.

sources.title: Use-by and best-before dates (page last updated 25 February 2025): foods that must be eaten before a certain time for health or safety reasons carry a use-by date and should not be eaten after it; foods can still be eaten for a while after the best-before date as they should be safe but may have lost some quality. Re-read 2026-10-29.

sources.title: Cooking temperatures (re-read 2026-10-30): cook minced meat, sausages and poultry right through to the centre; the page says what counts as pink or clear juices differs from person to person and colour is not always a reliable indicator, and advises a food thermometer. Safe temperatures table: minced meat and sausages 71 C; chicken and turkey (whole, thighs, wings, legs, breasts) 74 C; fish 63 C; leftovers 60 C. Poultry: probe in the inner thigh near the breast, not touching bone; ground meats and poultry dishes: thickest area.

sources.title: Poultry and raw meat: cook poultry, minced meats and sausages until well done, right through to the centre, no pink visible, juices clear; never wash raw chicken; keep raw meat and poultry apart from ready-to-eat food; refrigerate promptly. Read 2026-10-29.

sources.title: Eggs, enjoy safely (and the higher-risk dishes page): cook eggs until the white is completely firm and the yolk has started to thicken; people at greater risk (children under 2, pregnant women, people over 70, weakened immune system) should not eat raw or lightly cooked eggs. Read 2026-10-30.

steps: Boil the rice as the packet says.
Sauté the garlic, onion and tomato in the oil, then add the shredded cabbage.
Make a gap, scramble in the eggs, and stir together until the whites are completely firm.

recipes.name: Tomato and pepper eggs
recipes.blurb: Eggs set gently in a tomato and capsicum sauce, with bread.
steps: Soften the chopped onion and capsicum in the oil.
Add the tomato and cook until saucy.
Crack in the eggs and stir gently until the whites are completely firm and the yolks have started to thicken. Serve with bread.
recipes.basis: Author's own simple recipe: weights are for the whole recipe and nutrition is computed from them (raw or dry unless the food-table row says boiled or canned); cooking changes are not modelled. Salt and pepper are to taste and not counted, so sodium is not modelled.

recipes.name: Tomato bulgur pilaf
recipes.blurb: Bulgur cooked in a light tomato base.
steps: Soften the chopped onion and capsicum in the oil, then add the diced tomato.
Stir in the bulgur and enough water to just cover.
Cover and cook on low until the water is absorbed, then rest and fluff.
recipes.basis: Author's own simple recipe: weights are for the whole recipe and nutrition is computed from them (raw or dry unless the food-table row says boiled or canned); cooking changes are not modelled. Salt and pepper are to taste and not counted, so sodium is not modelled.

recipes.name: Eggplant and chickpea stew
recipes.blurb: Meatless eggplant simmered in tomato with chickpeas.
steps: Cube the eggplant and fry in the olive oil until golden.
Add the sliced onion and garlic, then the tomatoes.
Stir in the drained chickpeas and simmer until the eggplant is very soft.
recipes.basis: Author's own simple recipe: weights are for the whole recipe and nutrition is computed from them (raw or dry unless the food-table row says boiled or canned); cooking changes are not modelled. Salt and pepper are to taste and not counted, so sodium is not modelled.

recipes.name: Coconut dhal
recipes.blurb: Red lentils cooked in coconut milk with turmeric.
steps: Simmer the rinsed lentils with the turmeric in water until soft.
Add the coconut milk, chopped onion, garlic and chilli.
Simmer gently until the lentils are creamy.
recipes.basis: Author's own simple recipe: weights are for the whole recipe and nutrition is computed from them (raw or dry unless the food-table row says boiled or canned); cooking changes are not modelled. Salt and pepper are to taste and not counted, so sodium is not modelled.

recipes.name: Green bean coconut curry
recipes.blurb: Green beans simmered in a mild coconut sauce.
steps: Trim the beans and cut into short lengths.
Put everything in a pot with a splash of water.
Simmer gently until the beans are tender and the sauce is thick.

recipes.blurb: Soft pumpkin cooked in coconut milk with a little chilli.
steps: Peel the pumpkin and cut into chunks.
Put it in a pot with the onion, garlic, turmeric, chilli, coconut milk and a splash of water.
Simmer until the pumpkin is soft and the sauce is thick.

swapRecipes.blurb: Chicken and vegetable nuggets, fried until golden, with a garlicky yoghurt dip.
steps: Chop the spinach, spring onion and parsley (keep some parsley for the dip) and grate the zucchini and carrot.
Mix the chicken mince with the vegetables and most of the garlic.
Shape the mixture into small flat nuggets.
Fry the nuggets in the oil over medium heat, turning, until golden on both sides.
Check with a food thermometer in the thickest part of a nugget. Chicken needs 74°C. No pink inside is only a second sign.
Stir the rest of the garlic and parsley through the yoghurt for a dip.

swapRecipes.blurb: Beef mince and grated vegetables rolled in puff pastry and baked.
steps: Heat the oven to hot. Grate the carrot, pumpkin and zucchini and finely chop the onion, garlic and walnuts.
Mix the beef mince with the vegetables and walnuts.
Cut the pastry into strips, spoon the mixture along each strip, then roll up and seal the edge.
Bake the rolls on a lined tray until the pastry is puffed and golden.
Check with a food thermometer in the middle of a roll. Minced meat needs 71°C. No pink inside is only a second sign.

swapRecipes.blurb: Mashed sweet potato, lentils and spinach pan-fried into soft patties.
steps: Peel and cube the sweet potato, boil until soft, drain and mash.
Chop the spinach. Use lentils that are already cooked (boiled, or tinned and drained).
Mix the mash, lentils, spinach, flour, cumin and paprika.
Shape into patties.
Fry the patties in the oil over medium heat until golden on both sides and hot right through.

swapRecipes.blurb: Chicken, bok choy, broccoli and carrot stir-fried with ginger, on brown rice.
steps: Cook the brown rice as the packet says, drain and keep warm.
Slice the chicken thinly. Cut the vegetables into small pieces and grate the ginger.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil over high heat until browned, adding the ginger, a little garlic and a pinch of chilli near the end.
Check with a food thermometer in the thickest piece. Chicken needs 74°C. No pink inside is only a second sign.
Add the vegetables and soy sauce with a splash of water and toss until tender but still bright. Finish with a few drops of sesame oil and vinegar.
Serve over the rice.

swapRecipes.blurb: Pork mince and chopped vegetables spooned into crisp lettuce cups.
steps: Finely chop the carrot, onion, capsicum and water chestnuts. Separate the lettuce leaves into cups.
Fry the pork mince in the sesame oil over high heat, breaking it up, until browned.
Check with a food thermometer in the thickest part. Minced meat needs 71°C. No pink inside is only a second sign.
Stir in the vegetables, garlic, soy sauce and a little grated ginger and chilli, and stir-fry until just tender.
Spoon into the lettuce cups and top with chopped spring onion and coriander.

swapRecipes.blurb: Spiced beef and tomato over corn chips, warmed in the oven, with sour cream.
steps: Brown the beef mince in a frying pan over medium-high heat, breaking it up.
Check with a food thermometer in the thickest part. Minced meat needs 71°C. No pink inside is only a second sign.
Stir in the tinned tomatoes and taco seasoning and simmer until thick.
Spread the corn chips on a tray, spoon the beef over them and warm in a hot oven until hot right through.
Serve with the sour cream on top.

swapRecipes.blurb: Soft tortillas filled with shredded chicken, beans, salad and avocado.
steps: Shred cooked chicken breast that has been kept in the fridge, then warm it in a pan until steaming hot.
Drain and rinse the beans. Slice the avocado, tomato and cucumber, tear the lettuce and grate the cheese.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until soft.
Fill each tortilla with chicken, beans, salad, avocado and cheese, add a few thin slices of red onion if you have it, and top with a spoonful of sour cream.

swapRecipes.blurb: Chewy oat and coconut biscuits sweetened with golden syrup. Six biscuits.
steps: Heat the oven to moderate and line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the flour, sugar, oats and coconut in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together, then stir in a little bicarbonate of soda mixed with a splash of hot water.
Pour into the dry mix and stir to a stiff dough, then roll into balls and flatten them on the tray with room to spread.
Bake until golden brown, then cool on the tray. They crisp up as they cool.

swapRecipes.blurb: Soft biscuits of oats, dates, carrot and banana. Six biscuits.
steps: Heat the oven to moderate and line a tray with baking paper.
Chop the dates and almonds, grate the carrot and mash the banana.
Whisk one egg and use about half. Beat it with the oil and brown sugar, then stir in the banana, carrot, dates, almonds, oats, flour and a little cinnamon.
Spoon into six mounds on the tray and flatten them a little.
Bake until the biscuits are golden and firm and the egg is completely cooked.

swapRecipes.blurb: A thick banana, blueberry and yoghurt smoothie made with milk.
steps: Break the banana into chunks and put it in a blender with the frozen blueberries.
Add the yoghurt and milk.
Blend until smooth, adding a splash more milk if it is too thick. Drink soon, or keep it in the fridge and drink it the same day.

swapRecipes.blurb: Strawberries, yoghurt and milk blended into a quick pink smoothie.
steps: Wash the strawberries and cut off the green tops.
Put them in a blender with the yoghurt and milk.
Blend until smooth. Drink soon, or keep it in the fridge and drink it the same day.

swapRecipes.blurb: Chunky avocado, tomato and corn salsa with crisp baked pita wedges.
steps: Heat the oven to moderate. Cut the pita into wedges, spread them on a tray and bake until crisp and lightly golden.
Chop the tomato, chilli, coriander and red onion finely and drain the corn.
Mash the avocado roughly with a fork and stir in the chopped salad and the corn.
Serve the salsa with the pita chips. Eat it the same day, as avocado darkens.

swapRecipes.blurb: Almonds baked with honey and cinnamon for a small crunchy handful.
steps: Heat the oven to moderate and line a tray with baking paper.
Warm the honey and oil together, then stir in the cinnamon and toss the almonds through until coated.
Spread the nuts in one layer and bake, stirring once, until they smell toasty and look lightly golden.
Cool completely on the tray, then break up any clumps and keep in a jar.

swapRecipes.blurb: Banana, pineapple, passionfruit and yoghurt spooned out and frozen into cool bites.
steps: Mash the banana well with a fork, then stir in the yoghurt until smooth.
Drain the pineapple lightly and fold it through with the passionfruit pulp.
Spoon small mounds onto a lined tray, or into a mini muffin tray.
Freeze until firm, a few hours or overnight, then move them to a container and keep them frozen.

swapRecipes.blurb: Egg baked in a muffin tray with capsicum, carrot and mushroom. Two per serve.
steps: Heat the oven to moderate and grease a six-hole muffin tray. Grate the carrot and finely chop the capsicum and mushrooms.
Beat the eggs in a jug and stir in the vegetables and a little pepper.
Pour the mixture evenly into the six holes.
Bake until puffed and the eggs are cooked until completely firm all the way through. Cool a little before lifting out.

swapRecipes.blurb: Hard-boiled egg mashed with mayonnaise, rolled up in flatbread with hummus and salad.
steps: Put the eggs in a pot of cold water, bring to the boil and simmer until the eggs are completely firm right through, white and yolk. Cool in cold water.
Peel and mash the eggs with the mayonnaise.
Grate the carrot, slice the cucumber into strips and shred the spinach.
Spread the hummus over each flatbread, add the egg, then the vegetables and roll up tightly. Cut in half.

swapRecipes.blurb: A small, soft banana loaf with dates and a little wholemeal flour. Cut into six slices.
steps: Heat the oven to moderate and line a small loaf tin with baking paper. Chop the dates.
Mash the bananas well, then beat in about three-quarters of a beaten egg, the milk and the oil.
Stir in both flours, the cinnamon and the dates until just mixed.
Spoon into the tin and bake until a skewer comes out clean and the egg is cooked until completely firm. Cool before slicing.

swapRecipes.blurb: Thick banana and blueberry pikelets cooked in a pan. Makes a stack for six.
steps: Mash the banana well, then whisk in the milk and about three-quarters of a beaten egg.
Stir in the flour until just combined, then fold through the blueberries.
Heat a non-stick pan with a thin film of oil on medium heat and drop in spoonfuls of batter.
Cook until bubbles show, flip, and cook until golden with the egg completely firm in the middle. Keep warm while you cook the rest.

swapRecipes.blurb: Yoghurt dough spread with tomato paste, vegetables and cheese, rolled and baked.
steps: Heat the oven to moderate and line a tray. Finely chop the tomato, capsicum and red onion.
Mix both flours with the yoghurt and a splash of milk to a soft dough, then roll it into a rectangle.
Spread with tomato paste, scatter over the vegetables, cheese and a pinch of oregano, then roll up from the long side.
Cut into six slices, lay them flat on the tray and bake until golden and the cheese is bubbling.

swapRecipes.blurb: Pasta in a creamy tomato sauce full of grated and chopped vegetables.
steps: Cook the pasta as the packet says, drain and keep warm.
Grate the carrot and sweet potato and chop the zucchini and tomato. Chop the capsicum and cauliflower small, with a little garlic.
Soften the garlic and vegetables in the oil in a large pan, then add the pasta sauce and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the milk and sour cream, warm through without boiling, then mix through the pasta and top with the cheese.

swapRecipes.blurb: Chicken, zucchini and tomato tossed through penne with a fresh basil and parmesan pesto.
steps: Cook the pasta as the packet says, drain and keep warm.
Chop the basil very finely and mix with the grated parmesan, chopped pine nuts and a little oil to make a rough pesto.
Cut the chicken into small pieces and fry in the oil over medium-high heat with the onion, a little garlic and chilli until browned.
Check with a food thermometer in the thickest piece. Chicken needs 74°C. No pink inside is only a second sign.
Add the zucchini, tomato and spinach and stir until the spinach wilts, then toss through the pasta and pesto with a little chopped parsley.

swapRecipes.blurb: Crisp tofu and plenty of vegetables stir-fried with soba noodles and soy sauce.
steps: Cook the soba noodles as the packet says, drain and rinse.
Pat the tofu dry, cut into cubes and toss in a little cornflour. Cut the vegetables into thin strips.
Fry the tofu in a hot pan with a little sesame oil until golden, then lift out.
Stir-fry the onion and hard vegetables with the garlic, ginger and chilli, then add the soft vegetables, noodles, tofu, soy sauce and a little honey.
Toss until hot and top with chopped coriander.

swapRecipes.blurb: Pumpkin and chickpeas simmered in coconut milk and tomato, served over rice.
steps: Cook the rice as the packet says, drain and keep warm.
Cut the pumpkin into small cubes and chop the onion. Chop the chilli, garlic and ginger.
Soften the onion in the oil, then stir in the garlic, ginger, chilli, turmeric, cumin and ground coriander until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk, pumpkin and chickpeas and simmer until the pumpkin is soft.
Serve over the rice with chopped coriander.

notFound: Swap recipes not made into Cook recipes: baked-fish-capsicum (sample cost about $5.80 a serve, above the $4.00 Cook limit) and beef-taco-roll (13 ingredient rows; only olive oil, tomato paste and taco seasoning are minor seasonings, so at most 3 can be uncounted and 10 rows would be counted, above the limit of 9). Both were re-checked on 2026-11-25 and still break those limits.

Soak-and-boil dried bean recipes (including dried chickpeas, haricot and kidney beans) are not shipped: no official boiling or soaking source was read. Canned beans, chickpeas and split lentils are used instead.
Raw seafood and raw fish recipes are not shipped; only fully cooked or tinned fish (tinned tuna and salmon) is used. No official source for cooking fish at home was recorded for the recipes.

NSW Food Authority "Food risk and you: what to eat with a weakened immune system" (PDF, https://www.foodauthority.nsw.gov.au/media/8789) downloaded but its text could not be extracted (embedded fonts), so it was not read and the pregnancy and immune-system line stays omitted.

Victorian Department of Health and Better Health Channel pages for cooking chicken and leftovers returned 404 (health.vic.gov.au/food-safety/cook-chicken, betterhealth.vic.gov.au food-safety-and-chicken); the NSW Food Authority pages are used instead and are labelled NSW.
FSANZ pages /consumer/safety/food-safety-tips and /consumer/safety/poultry returned 404 and were not read.
Curry powder (AFCD F003337) and tomato paste, soy sauce and fish sauce were not added: blends and sauces have no read source for diet flags, so recipes use single spices and leave sauces out.

Prices are sample estimates of a typical Melbourne supermarket price per kg, rounded to 10c; no price source was read. Tinned goods are priced per kg of the weight used in the recipe (drained where the nutrition row is drained).
Frozen peas use the AFCD row "Pea, green, frozen, boiled, drained" because the workbook has no raw frozen-pea row; the peas are only heated through in recipes.
Cooked-weight rows: rice noodles use the boiled AFCD row, so the recipe grams are cooked weight; all other grains and pasta use dry rows. Cooking changes are not modelled and salt is not counted.
Recipe wording is the author's own; no third-party recipe text was used. A food-safety or dietitian review of the recipes is still recommended.

Halal, kosher, vegan and gluten flags for packaged goods (bread, cheddar, baked beans, tinned fish, frozen peas, tinned corn and beans) stay unknown or partial as in the cultural table; no product-specific source was read.
chicken-mince has no stated figure on the NSW cooking-temperatures table (it lists chicken cuts at 74 C and minced meat at 71 C); the higher 74 C is required for it. No recipe uses chicken mince yet.
